clue.text: A shocking twister?

parts.note: a creature that wriggles like a twisting rope and delivers an electric shock to its prey

explanation.definitionFit: This South American fish is long and snakelike, so it twists, and it stuns prey with a strong electric discharge.

clue.text: Put down a pound to help

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from the Latin libra
to help is to give aid

explanation.surface: Someone sets a pound coin down as a contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, to place something down on a surface.

clue.text: One often confined in prison operates a big fiddle

definitions.text: One often confined in prison operates a big fiddle

parts.words: One often confined in prison operates a big fiddle
parts.note: reads as a convict running a large swindle, but describes a musician whose name begins with a word for a prison room and who plays the large bowed instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A player of the cello, the big member of the violin (fiddle) family, whose title starts with the word for a prison room.

clue.text: Rugby's finest hour in a Germany

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Rugby's finest hour in a Germany' is garbled by OCR: RU (Rugby) + HR (hour) gives the letters, but 'finest' has no job and 'in a Germany' cannot define a German region; the printed wording is not recoverable
annotationWithheld.clue: Rugby's finest hour in a Germany

clue.text: I can't be bothered where the ministers meet

indicators.note: bothered means upset or flustered, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A weary politician shrugs off going to the government meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I can't be bothered' reads as a shrug, but 'bothered' is the anagram signal for the seven letters of I CAN'T BE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet is the senior group of government ministers, and also the room in which they hold their meetings.

clue.text: She's called over a measure of cloth

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another sits above it in the column

parts.note: an ell is an old unit for measuring cloth, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: A woman is summoned to come across to a length of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' stacks the cloth measure above the single letter. The name also runs backwards inside 'called', a bonus touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a girl's given name, so it can stand for any woman referred to as she.

clue.text: The Dean's response to hasty words?

definitions.text: The Dean's response to hasty words?

parts.words: The Dean's response to hasty words?
parts.note: the Dean is Jonathan Swift, Dean of St Patrick's in Dublin, so his reply bears his surname; it also means a quick reply

explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, was Dean of St Patrick's Cathedral, Dublin, and is often called simply 'the Dean'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid retort is a quick reply, and a reply from Dean Jonathan Swift would carry his surname.

clue.text: Overfeed pelican but satisfy requirements

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a seabird yet still meets the brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffing a pelican's beak full is literally loading its bill, and the idiom means to meet what is needed or be suitable.

clue.text: Plundering occupation, but the footwear's a giveaway

explanation.surface: A looter's line of work is betrayed by the boots he wears.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy or looting is the trade of a buccaneer; read in two halves, boots handed out at no charge are footwear given away.

clue.text: In period of fast, odd modicum of time when all is understood

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the word for the fasting season

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: During a time of fasting, a small strange instant brings sudden clarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period of fast' is Lent, the Christian season before Easter; 'odd' jumbles 'modicum', and 'In' sets the result inside the fasting season's word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief spell of clear thinking, especially in someone otherwise confused, is a moment of clarity.

clue.text: A neat drink taken by the tot, naturally .

definitions.text: A neat drink taken by the tot, naturally .

parts.words: A neat drink taken by the tot, naturally .
parts.note: reads like a measure of undiluted spirit (a tot), but describes the drink a baby (a tot) takes from the breast

explanation.definitionFit: Breast milk is the natural, undiluted nourishment a nursing infant drinks.

clue.text: Part of a sentence that may be dropped advisedly

definitions.text: Part of a sentence that may be dropped advisedly

parts.words: Part of a sentence that may be dropped advisedly
parts.note: a unit of a sentence, and the thing one drops when giving a quiet hint, as in dropping one in someone's ear

explanation.definitionFit: Sentences are built of these units, and to drop one in someone's ear is to offer a discreet piece of advice.

clue.text: This graph could make somebody's name in the car industry

definitions.text: This graph could make somebody's name in the car industry

parts.words: This graph could make somebody's name in the car industry
parts.note: put before the word graph it forms a signature, a person's written name; on its own it is a word for a car

explanation.definitionFit: Placed before 'graph' it makes a signature, and on its own it is a short word for a motor car.

clue.text: Musical opening amid elfish characters from part of the Low Countries

definitions.text: from part of the Low Countries

indicators.note: amid places the single letter in among the jumbled letters
the letters (characters) of the word before it are taken as raw material to rearrange
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tune begins among some impish figures somewhere in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like a noun for people but signals an anagram of 'elfish'; 'amid' puts the first letter of 'Musical' inside it. Flemish is the Dutch spoken in Flanders, northern Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is the Dutch-speaking northern region of Belgium, and its people and language bear this adjective.

clue.text: … but hitch when I broach some German wine

indicators.note: to broach is to pierce into a cask, so the letter goes into the wine

parts.note: hock is a white wine from the Rhine region of Germany

explanation.surface: Something goes wrong when I open a bottle of Rhine wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is the British name for white Rhine wine; 'broach', as in tapping a cask, puts the letter I inside it. The leading dots carry on from the previous clue and do no work.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoick is to jerk or yank upward, just as to hitch is to pull up with a tug.

clue.text: Perhaps the bad-tempered hen is feeling a little hungry?

explanation.surface: A grumpy chicken turns out to want a bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen that keeps pecking is literally inclined to peck; in everyday speech the word means wanting a snack.

clue.text: Lamps adjusted for some singing in the services

indicators.note: adjusted means altered or rearranged, so the letters of the first word are reordered

explanation.surface: Lights are fixed up ready for the hymns at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song from the biblical book is often sung or chanted in church worship.

clue.text: A drink that goes well with the marmalade

explanation.surface: A drink is the perfect pairing for orange preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising glasses to someone is drinking their health, and crisp grilled bread is the usual partner for a breakfast preserve.

clue.text: Stratford stands by a blazing revolutionary star

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the star's word is read backwards

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares up, hence blazing

explanation.surface: A theatre town sits beside a dazzling rebellious celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blazing' describes the star: a nova suddenly flares in brightness. Stratford-upon-Avon is Shakespeare's birthplace in England, on this river.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's home town, Stratford, is sited on the banks of this English river.

clue.text: Thus Eastern prince called the tune around noon

indicators.note: the tune's word goes around the letter for noon

parts.note: an air is a melody or tune
M stands for meridies, noon, as in a.m. and p.m.

explanation.surface: So the Arab ruler decided what music was played at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thus' and 'called' are links; 'around' puts M after the A of AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amir, or emir, is a Muslim ruler or commander in the Middle East.

clue.text: Scrape a bed of oysters

explanation.surface: Scrape clean a stretch of shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: To scalp a surface is to shave or scrape it bare, and in Scots the same word names a bank where shellfish grow.

clue.text: One who moves smartly to score afresh

indicators.note: afresh means anew, so the letters of the phrase are set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone darts about trying to put points on the board again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scoots dashes off quickly, so one who moves briskly fits.

clue.text: It adds weight to the aircraft's profit balance, too

definitions.text: It adds weight to the aircraft's profit balance, too

parts.words: It adds weight to the aircraft's profit balance, too
parts.note: the cargo a plane carries is extra weight, and it is the part of the load that earns money

explanation.definitionFit: The paying cargo or passengers an aircraft carries add to its weight and are what generate revenue.

clue.text: Reverse command to a slip, ped-disc sufferer's osteopath?

definitions.text: command to a slip, ped-disc sufferer's osteopath

explanation.surface: A misfortune, or what a bone doctor is told to do for a slipped disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or misfortune; an osteopath treating a slipped disc might be told to put the patient's spine in place.

clue.text: The degree that can't be surpassed

definitions.text: The degree that can't be surpassed

parts.words: The degree that can't be surpassed
parts.note: the greatest possible amount or level, the top limit

explanation.definitionFit: The highest possible amount or extent is the one nothing can exceed.

clue.text: Nose out some great ages

indicators.note: out means unsettled or wrong, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sniff out a few long periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immeasurably long period, so several of them are great ages.

clue.text: Library centre in bishop's province is reverse of flourishing

indicators.note: in places the middle letter inside the word for a bishop's area

parts.note: a see is the diocese of a bishop

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

explanation.surface: A cathedral library's middle section is anything but thriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere means dried up and withered, the opposite of thriving growth.

clue.text: A garden runner and climber has been known to jump too

definitions.text: A garden runner and climber has been known to jump too

parts.words: A garden runner and climber has been known to jump too
parts.note: a runner and a climbing plant in the garden; the Mexican variety jumps because of a moth larva inside

explanation.definitionFit: The runner variety climbs garden poles, and the Mexican jumping kind hops about because of a larva inside.

clue.text: Dye extracted from an illegal plant

indicators.note: extracted from says the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Colouring obtained from a banned plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it.

clue.text: Article we turn up all over again

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up reads it from bottom to top

explanation.surface: We arrive with an object once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means afresh, once more from the start.

clue.text: Understand fencing?

explanation.surface: Grasp the meaning of swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp what is meant is to see what someone is driving at; in fencing, the sword's tip is what an opponent receives.

clue.text: Poor Abe drowning as the pressure is weighing heavily

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters of the words after it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Poor Abe is drowning under heavy pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as the pressure is' is link padding leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert heavy downward pressure, as a woman in labour or a burden does, is to press down hard.
